claim: Many different functions are regulated by circadian rhythms, including those orchestrated by discrete clock neurons within animal brains.
source: Many different functions are regulated by circadian rhythms, including those orchestrated by discrete clock neurons within animal brains.
evidence: This is a general statement about circadian rhythms that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Drosophila has 75 pairs of circadian neurons.
source: To comprehensively characterize and assign cell identity to the 75 pairs of Drosophila circadian neurons, we optimized a single-cell RNA sequencing method and assayed clock neuron gene expression at different times of day.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila circadian neuron anatomy.

claim: The study identified at least 17 clock neuron categories.
source: The data identify at least 17 clock neuron categories with striking spatial regulation of gene expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clustering analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Clock neuron categories show striking spatial regulation of gene expression.
source: The data identify at least 17 clock neuron categories with striking spatial regulation of gene expression.
evidence: This is supported by the differential gene expression analysis across clusters.

claim: Transcription factor regulation is prominent in clock neurons.
source: Transcription factor regulation is prominent and likely contributes to the robust circadian oscillation of many transcripts, including those that encode cell-surface proteins previously shown to be important for cell recognition and synapse formation during development.
evidence: This is supported by the identification of enriched transcription factors in the clusters.

claim: Transcription factor regulation likely contributes to the robust circadian oscillation of many transcripts.
source: Transcription factor regulation is prominent and likely contributes to the robust circadian oscillation of many transcripts, including those that encode cell-surface proteins previously shown to be important for cell recognition and synapse formation during development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed TF expression patterns and cycling transcripts.

claim: Cell-surface proteins important for cell recognition and synapse formation during development show circadian oscillation.
source: Transcription factor regulation is prominent and likely contributes to the robust circadian oscillation of many transcripts, including those that encode cell-surface proteins previously shown to be important for cell recognition and synapse formation during development.
evidence: This is supported by the cycling analysis of DIP, Dpr, and Beat family genes.

claim: Eukaryotic circadian clocks rely on a transcription-translation feedback loop that generates roughly ~24 hr periodicity.
source: Eukaryotic circadian clocks rely on a now well-defined transcription-translation feedback loop, which generates roughly ~24 hr periodicity (Takahashi, 2017; Top and Young, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Circadian transcription factors drive the oscillating expression of many thousands of tissue-specific output genes.
source: Importantly, these circadian transcription factors (TFs) drive the oscillating expression of many thousands of tissue-specific output genes, which regulate diverse aspects of physiology and behavior (Meireles-Filho et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) in the anteroventral hypothalamus has very strong core clock gene expression.
source: The brain clock is most apparent – has very strong core clock gene expression – in a restricted region of the anteroventral hypothalamus, the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) (Reppert and Moore, 1991).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: There are approximately 10,000 neurons in each unilateral mice SCN.
source: There are approximately 10,000 neurons in each unilateral mice SCN.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about the mouse SCN.

claim: The comparable region in Drosophila contains about 75 clock neurons on each hemisphere of the fly brain.
source: The comparable region in Drosophila contains about 75 clock neurons on each hemisphere of the fly brain.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about Drosophila.

claim: The SCN in mammals and the 75 pairs of neurons in flies orchestrate many circadian functions, including behaviors.
source: The SCN in mammals and these 75 pairs of neurons in flies orchestrate many circadian functions, including behaviors (Allada and Chung, 2010; Siepka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Fly brain clock neurons have been principally classified based on anatomy.
source: The fly brain clock neurons have been principally classified based on anatomy.
evidence: This is established knowledge about how clock neurons have been traditionally classified.

claim: There are lateral neurons and dorsal neurons in the fly brain clock system.
source: There are lateral neurons and dorsal neurons.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The lateral neurons are separated into three groups: ventral lateral neurons (nine LNvs), dorsal lateral neurons (six LNds), and lateral posterior neurons (three LPN).
source: The lateral neurons are separated into three groups: ventral lateral neurons (nine LNvs), dorsal lateral neurons (six LNds), and lateral posterior neurons (three LPN).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about clock neuron organization.

claim: The LNvs are further subdivided into large and small LNvs based on size and location, four l-LNvs and five s-LNvs, respectively.
source: The LNvs are further subdivided into large and small LNvs based on size and location, four l-LNvs and five s-LNvs, respectively.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The dorsal neurons are separated into four groups based on location: 15 DN1ps, 2 DN1as, 2 DN2s, and 35–40 DN3s.
source: The dorsal neurons constitute a much larger fraction of the 75 clock neurons and are also separated into four groups based on location: 15 DN1ps, 2 DN1as, 2 DN2s, and 35–40 DN3s (Shafer et al., 2006; Helfrich-Förster, 2004).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Different clock neuron groups are distinct by multiple criteria.
source: Not surprisingly perhaps, these different clock neuron groups are distinct by multiple criteria.
evidence: This is supported by the subsequent examples and citations provided.

claim: Calcium and functional assays indicate that different clock neurons are active at different times during a 24-hr cycle.
source: For example, calcium and functional assays indicate that different clock neurons are active at different times during a 24-hr cycle (Liang et al., 2016; Guo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Microarray and RNA sequencing studies indicate that different clock neuron groups express different sets of genes and transcripts.
source: Although microarray and RNA sequencing studies also indicate that different clock neuron groups express different sets of genes and transcripts (Abruzzi et al., 2017; Kula-Eversole et al., 2010; Nagoshi et al., 2010), the extent of gene expression heterogeneity is often underestimated by group sequencing.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The extent of gene expression heterogeneity is often underestimated by group sequencing.
source: Although microarray and RNA sequencing studies also indicate that different clock neuron groups express different sets of genes and transcripts (Abruzzi et al., 2017; Kula-Eversole et al., 2010; Nagoshi et al., 2010), the extent of gene expression heterogeneity is often underestimated by group sequencing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between bulk and single-cell sequencing approaches.

claim: An unsupervised clustering method confidently identified 17 clock neuron classes.
source: An unsupervised clustering method confidently identified 17 clock neuron classes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the computational analysis of the single-cell data.

claim: The 17 clusters were successfully mapped based on both known and novel marker genes to cover most if not all functionally distinct clock subgroups.
source: These clusters were successfully mapped based on both known and novel marker genes to cover most if not all functionally distinct clock subgroups.
evidence: This is supported by the marker gene analysis and validation experiments.

claim: Cell-type-specific enriched and oscillating transcripts were identified by differential gene expression.
source: Cell-type-specific enriched and oscillating transcripts were identified by differential gene expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the differential expression and cycling analysis.

claim: Circadian regulation of cell-surface molecules includes those previously shown to be important for cell recognition and synapse formation during development.
source: Strikingly, they include cell-surface molecules, previously shown to be important for cell recognition and synapse formation during development.
evidence: This is supported by the identification of cycling DIP, Dpr, and Beat family genes and citations to developmental studies.

claim: Circadian regulation of specificity molecules may orchestrate the temporal regulation of synapse formation and/or strength within the circadian network or between this network and other locations in the adult nervous system.
source: We suggest that the circadian regulation of these specificity molecules orchestrate the temporal regulation of synapse formation and/or strength within the circadian network or between this network and other locations in the adult nervous system.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cycling cell-surface molecule data.

claim: Clk856-GAL4 was used to express EGFP in most adult brain clock neurons.
source: The clock neuron driver Clk856-GAL4 was used to express EGFP in most adult brain clock neurons (Gummadova et al., 2009), which were indeed GFP- and TIM (TIMELESS) -positive (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the citation and the immunostaining data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Most if not all neurons in every clock neuron group were GFP-positive, with the exception of DN3s with 30% GFP-positive neurons.
source: Notably, most if not all neurons in every group were GFP-positive; the only exception was the DN3s with 30% GFP-positive neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the quantification shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There were approximately seven ectopic GFP-positive cells in each hemisphere that were TIM-negative by immunohistochemistry.
source: There were also approximately seven ectopic GFP-positive cells in each hemisphere; they were TIM-negative by immunohistochemistry (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining and quantification data.

claim: Cell-specific knock-down of critical clock components with Clk856-GAL4 mimics the phenotypes of classic circadian mutant lines.
source: Cell-specific knock-down of critical clock components with Clk856-GAL4 mimics the phenotypes of classic circadian mutant lines (Schlichting et al., 2019), consistent with the notion that the GFP-positive cells identify many functionally important clock neurons.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The GFP-positive cells identify many functionally important clock neurons.
source: Cell-specific knock-down of critical clock components with Clk856-GAL4 mimics the phenotypes of classic circadian mutant lines (Schlichting et al., 2019), consistent with the notion that the GFP-positive cells identify many functionally important clock neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional validation cited.

claim: The single-cell sequencing method was optimized based on CEL-Seq2.
source: We optimized this method for Drosophila clock neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) by using two rounds of in vitro transcriptions to amplify polyA RNA (Paul et al., 2017).
evidence: This is described in the methods and supported by citation.

claim: Each cell was sequenced to a depth of about 0.5 million reads.
source: Each cell was sequenced to a depth of about 0.5 million reads, and approximately 2300 cells from LD- and DD-entrained flies passed the stringent filtering criteria for a total of 4671 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a description of the sequencing depth achieved in the study.

claim: Approximately 2300 cells from LD-entrained flies and 2300 cells from DD-entrained flies passed stringent filtering criteria for a total of 4671 cells.
source: Each cell was sequenced to a depth of about 0.5 million reads, and approximately 2300 cells from LD- and DD-entrained flies passed the stringent filtering criteria for a total of 4671 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There were about 2600 genes detected per cell (mean) with an average of about eight UMIs per gene.
source: There were about 2600 genes detected per cell (mean) with an average of about eight UMIs (unique molecular identifiers; about 20,000 UMIs total).
evidence: This is a description of the sequencing quality metrics.

claim: Only a few genes and UMIs were detected in empty wells.
source: This indicates deep molecular characterization as only a few genes and UMIs were detected in empty wells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the negative control data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Pearson correlation between corresponding replicates demonstrates that the sequencing data are highly reproducible.
source: The Pearson correlation between the corresponding replicates demonstrates that the sequencing data are highly reproducible, and even the Pearson correlation between LD and DD is 0.97, indicating highly similar gene expression between these two conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The Pearson correlation between LD and DD is 0.97, indicating highly similar gene expression between these two conditions.
source: The Pearson correlation between the corresponding replicates demonstrates that the sequencing data are highly reproducible, and even the Pearson correlation between LD and DD is 0.97, indicating highly similar gene expression between these two conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Unsupervised clustering with Seurat resulted in 39 distinct clusters.
source: We next integrated together the cells collected in LD and DD conditions cross different times of day by unsupervised clustering with Seurat (Butler et al., 2018), which resulted in 39 distinct clusters (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Every cluster contains cells from all six time points and from both LD- and DD-entrained flies with only modest variability.
source: Every cluster contains cells from all six time points and from both LD- and DD-entrained flies with only modest variability (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: There is much more variability in the number of cells per cluster.
source: There is, however, much more variability in the number of cells per cluster, and they are numbered based on the number of cells they include: 0 has the most cells, 38 the least (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: There are similar numbers of genes and UMIs per cell in each cluster.
source: Nonetheless, there are similar numbers of genes and UMIs per cell in each cluster (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Every cluster except cluster 0 shows a unique marker gene expression profile.
source: Moreover, every cluster except cluster 0 shows a unique marker gene expression profile, supporting the validity of even the smallest clusters (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 1E.

claim: tim mRNA is cycling with a gene expression peak at ZT14-ZT18 in most if not all clusters.
source: As expected, tim mRNA is cycling with a gene expression peak at ZT14-ZT18 in most if not all clusters (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the cycling data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There is a marked difference in the tim expression levels per cell among the different clusters.
source: There is, however, a marked difference in the tim and vri expression levels per cell among the different clusters.
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Clusters with more cells generally show considerably higher clock gene expression per cell.
source: Despite a few exceptional clusters, those with more cells generally show considerably higher clock gene expression per cell (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Clk expression at its usual LD peak time of ZT2 is higher in almost all of the same clusters that show high tim expression.
source: Clk expression at its usual LD peak time of ZT2 is similarly higher in almost all of these same clusters (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Higher levels of Clk and CLK-CYC direct target genes may identify bona fide circadian clock neurons.
source: Based on the notion that higher levels of Clk and CLK-CYC direct target genes may identify bona fide circadian clock neurons and to focus on a smaller number of clusters, we chose 17 for analysis in more detail (Figure 2; purple boxes).
evidence: This is a rationale based on established knowledge about clock gene function.

claim: Pdf is expressed in just eight clock cells and two cell types, the four large and four small LNvs on each side of the brain.
source: To identify lateral neuron clusters, we first addressed the expression of the famous circadian neuropeptide gene Pdf. It is expressed in just eight clock cells and two cell types, the four large and four small LNvs on each side of the brain; they are classically referred to as l-LNvs and s-LNvs, respectively (Helfrich-Forster, 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Pdf is expressed in only two clusters, 2 and 25.
source: Pdf is expressed in only two clusters, 2 and 25 (Figure 3B); cluster 2 but not cluster 25 also expresses substantial levels of sNPF mRNA (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: Cluster 2 but not cluster 25 also expresses substantial levels of sNPF mRNA.
source: Pdf is expressed in only two clusters, 2 and 25 (Figure 3B); cluster 2 but not cluster 25 also expresses substantial levels of sNPF mRNA (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: sNPF is expressed in s-LNvs but not l-LNvs.
source: As sNPF is expressed in s-LNvs but not l-LNvs (Johard et al., 2009), these data suggest that cluster 2 identifies s-LNvs and cluster 25 identifies l-LNvs.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Cluster 2 identifies s-LNvs and cluster 25 identifies l-LNvs.
source: As sNPF is expressed in s-LNvs but not l-LNvs (Johard et al., 2009), these data suggest that cluster 2 identifies s-LNvs and cluster 25 identifies l-LNvs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Pdf and sNPF expression patterns and prior knowledge.

claim: The s-LNv cluster 2 has many more cells than the l-LNv cluster 25 despite the fact that each fly brain has the same number of s-LNvs and l-LNvs.
source: The s-LNv cluster 2 has many more cells than the l-LNv cluster 25 despite the fact that each fly brain has the same number of s-LNvs and l-LNvs (see Discussion).
evidence: This is an observation from the clustering results that is noted as requiring discussion.

claim: One LNd and the fifth s-LNv express ion transport peptide (ITP).
source: One LNd and the fifth s-LNv express ion transport peptide (ITP) (Johard et al., 2009; Schubert et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ITP mRNA identifies only a single cluster, #8.
source: As ITP mRNA identifies only a single cluster, #8 (Figure 3D), we named it LN_ITP and suggest that it contains these two cells, the fifth s-LNv and this single LNd.
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cluster 8 (LN_ITP) contains the fifth s-LNv and one LNd.
source: As ITP mRNA identifies only a single cluster, #8 (Figure 3D), we named it LN_ITP and suggest that it contains these two cells, the fifth s-LNv and this single LNd.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ITP expression pattern and prior knowledge.

claim: A single cluster for the fifth s-LNv and one LNd implies that the transcript composition of these two neurons is very similar.
source: A single cluster implies that the transcript composition of these two neurons is very similar, consistent with their indistinguishable functional and connectivity properties (Yao and Shafer, 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the clustering result and supported by citation.

claim: The fifth s-LNv and one LNd have indistinguishable functional and connectivity properties.
source: A single cluster implies that the transcript composition of these two neurons is very similar, consistent with their indistinguishable functional and connectivity properties (Yao and Shafer, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: sNPF is expressed in two LNd cells in addition to the s-LNvs.
source: The neuropeptide sNPF is expressed in two LNd cells in addition to the s-LNvs (Johard et al., 2009), and this transcript is well-expressed in clusters 5 and 18 as well as in the s-LNv cluster 2 as described above (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: sNPF transcript is well-expressed in clusters 5 and 18 as well as in the s-LNv cluster 2.
source: The neuropeptide sNPF is expressed in two LNd cells in addition to the s-LNvs (Johard et al., 2009), and this transcript is well-expressed in clusters 5 and 18 as well as in the s-LNv cluster 2 as described above (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Cluster 18 is identified as a dorsal neuron cluster.
source: Cluster 18 is identified as a dorsal neuron cluster (see below).
evidence: This is stated as a finding that is explained later in the manuscript.

claim: Cluster 5 has prominent expression of the neuropeptide Trissin.
source: Cluster 5 has prominent expression of another neuropeptide, Trissin (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: A chemoconnectome Trissin endogenous GAL4 knock-in line resulted in expression in two LNds.
source: A chemoconnectome Trissin endogenous GAL4 knock-in line (Deng et al., 2019) resulted in expression in two LNds (Figure 3F), and an intersectional assay combining Trissin-LexA with Clk856-GAL4 also expressed only in these two LNds (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: An intersectional assay combining Trissin-LexA with Clk856-GAL4 expressed only in two LNds.
source: A chemoconnectome Trissin endogenous GAL4 knock-in line (Deng et al., 2019) resulted in expression in two LNds (Figure 3F), and an intersectional assay combining Trissin-LexA with Clk856-GAL4 also expressed only in these two LNds (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: TIM immunostaining signal co-localized with GFP in Trissin-expressing neurons and confirmed that these neurons are LNds.
source: In both these experiments, the TIM immunostaining signal co-localized with GFP and further confirmed that these neurons are LNds (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cluster 5 is named LNd_Trissin and contains two cells.
source: Based on these data, we named this two-cell cluster 5:LNd_Trissin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Trissin expression and validation experiments.

claim: Clusters 9 and 12 are most similar to the two previously defined lateral neuron clusters, LN_ITP and LNd_Trissin.
source: To identify the remaining three LNds, we examined gene expression similarity to find clusters most similar to the two previously defined lateral neuron clusters, LN_ITP and LNd_Trissin. These are clusters 9 and 12 (Figure 3G; blue box).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: AstC-R2 mRNA is well-expressed in clusters 9 and 12.
source: The transcript encoding the AstC receptor, AstC-R2 mRNA is well-expressed in these two clusters (Figure 3H) and in LNds based on previous RNA sequencing and physiology experiments (Abruzzi et al., 2017; Díaz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3H and citations.

claim: AstC-R2 is expressed in LNds based on previous RNA sequencing and physiology experiments.
source: The transcript encoding the AstC receptor, AstC-R2 mRNA is well-expressed in these two clusters (Figure 3H) and in LNds based on previous RNA sequencing and physiology experiments (Abruzzi et al., 2017; Díaz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: NPF is expressed in two LNds that are AstC-R2 positive.
source: Because NPF is also expressed in two LNds that are AstC-R2 positive (Lee et al., 2006), this explains the presence of NPF in cluster 9, which must contain these two cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Cluster 9 contains two NPF-expressing LNds.
source: Because NPF is also expressed in two LNds that are AstC-R2 positive (Lee et al., 2006), this explains the presence of NPF in cluster 9, which must contain these two cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on NPF expression and prior knowledge.

claim: NPF is upregulated in most of the clusters in DD.
source: We noticed NPF is upregulated in most of the clusters in DD, for cluster classification, NPF expression in LD condition is shown in Figure 3I.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: Cluster 12 contains the remaining single LNd.
source: By elimination, cluster 12 must contain the remaining single LNd.
evidence: This is an inference based on the process of elimination.

claim: Cluster 9 is named LNd_NPF and cluster 12 is named LNd.
source: Therefore, we have named these two clusters 9: LNd_NPF and 12: LNd.
evidence: This is a naming convention based on the marker gene analysis.

claim: The two DN1a neurons are the only source of CCHa1 in the fly clock system.
source: The two DN1a neurons are the only source of CCHa1 in the fly clock system (Fujiwara et al., 2018), and immunohistochemistry of a chemoconnectome CCHa1 line indicates that this gene is indeed expressed in only two clock neurons at the expected location for DN1as (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation and validated by immunostaining.

claim: Only cluster 3 expresses high levels of CCHa1.
source: As only cluster 3 expresses high levels of CCHa1, we assigned the two DN1as to this cluster (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The two DN1as are assigned to cluster 3.
source: As only cluster 3 expresses high levels of CCHa1, we assigned the two DN1as to this cluster (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an inference based on CCHa1 expression.

claim: DN2 molecular oscillations are in anti-phase with the rest of the clock neuron population in DD.
source: For DN2 neuron assignment, we took advantage of the fact that DN2 molecular oscillations are in anti-phase with the rest of the clock neuron population in DD (Kaneko et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Only cluster 19 shows unambiguous anti-phasic DD cycling for core clock genes including tim and vri.
source: Remarkably, only cluster 19 shows unambiguous anti-phasic DD cycling for a number of core clock genes including tim (Figure 2 and Figure 4B) and vri (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), justifying the assignment of the DN2s to cluster 19.
evidence: This is supported by the cycling data shown in Figure 2, Figure 4B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The DN2s are assigned to cluster 19.
source: Remarkably, only cluster 19 shows unambiguous anti-phasic DD cycling for a number of core clock genes including tim (Figure 2 and Figure 4B) and vri (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), justifying the assignment of the DN2s to cluster 19.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anti-phasic cycling pattern.

claim: The three LPNs are the only clock neuron group with both AstC and AstA expression.
source: The three LPNs are the only clock neuron group with both AstC and AstA expression (Díaz et al., 2019; Ni et al., 2019); only the small cluster 29 meets this criterion (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and expression data.

claim: Only cluster 29 expresses both AstC and AstA.
source: The three LPNs are the only clock neuron group with both AstC and AstA expression (Díaz et al., 2019; Ni et al., 2019); only the small cluster 29 meets this criterion (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Cluster 29 is assigned to the LPNs.
source: The three LPNs are the only clock neuron group with both AstC and AstA expression (Díaz et al., 2019; Ni et al., 2019); only the small cluster 29 meets this criterion (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the AstC and AstA expression pattern.

claim: The glass (gl)-encoded TF is expressed in and necessary for the development of most DN1ps.
source: First, the glass (gl)-encoded TF is expressed in and necessary for the development of most DN1ps (Helfrich-Förster et al., 2001; Shafer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Five novel clusters (1, 6, 7, 15, and 18) express the gl transcript, suggesting that they contain DN1ps.
source: Five novel clusters (1, 6, 7, 15, and 18) express the gl transcript, suggesting that they contain DN1ps (Figure 4E; five of the six circles).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Cluster 18 is sNPF enriched.
source: Cluster 18 is sNPF enriched as shown above (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Clusters 1 and 15 express the transcript encoding the neuropeptide Dh31.
source: Second, two of these five clusters, clusters 1 and 15, express the transcript encoding the neuropeptide Dh31 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Dh31 is expressed in some DN1ps.
source: Previous results indicate that Dh31 is expressed in some DN1ps, and loss- and gain-of-function studies of Dh31 indicate that its expression within this set of clock neurons regulates fly sleep (Kunst et al., 2014; Goda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Dh31 expression within DN1ps regulates fly sleep.
source: Previous results indicate that Dh31 is expressed in some DN1ps, and loss- and gain-of-function studies of Dh31 indicate that its expression within this set of clock neurons regulates fly sleep (Kunst et al., 2014; Goda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Clusters 1 and 15 also express the transcript encoding the neuropeptide CNMa.
source: Third, these same two clusters also express the transcript encoding the neuropeptide CNMa (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: A chemoconnectome knock-in CNMa-GAL4 drives EGFP expression in TIM-positive neurons in the position of DN1ps.
source: To verify the assignment of these two CNMa clusters, we used a chemoconnectome knock-in CNMa-GAL4 to drive EGFP for immunohistochemistry. The only TIM-positive EGFP-positive neurons were in the position of DN1ps (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Six to eight EGFP-positive dorsal cells from CNMa-GAL4 overlapped well with the DN1p Clk4.1 driver, indicating that these two DN1p clusters contain about half the DN1ps.
source: These six to eight EGFP-positive dorsal cells overlapped well with the well-known DN1p Clk4.1 driver (Clk4.1M-LexA), indicating that these two DN1p clusters contain about half the DN1ps (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: AstC mRNA expression identified only a single DN1p cluster, the larger Dh31-positive and CNMa-positive cluster 1.
source: Fourth, expression of the neuropeptide gene AstC mRNA identified only a single DN1p cluster, the larger Dh31-positive and CNMa-positive cluster 1 (Figure 4D), an assignment that is consistent with recent work indicating that AstC is expressed in a subset of DN1ps (Díaz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4D and citation.

claim: AstC is expressed in a subset of DN1ps.
source: Fourth, expression of the neuropeptide gene AstC mRNA identified only a single DN1p cluster, the larger Dh31-positive and CNMa-positive cluster 1 (Figure 4D), an assignment that is consistent with recent work indicating that AstC is expressed in a subset of DN1ps (Díaz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Rh7 expression identified an additional 6th DN1p cluster, cluster 4.
source: Lastly, Rh7 expression identified an additional 6th DN1p cluster, cluster 4 (Figure 4E,H).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4E,H.

claim: Rh7 mRNA is present in cluster 4 as well as three others: the DN1as, DN2s, and the gl-positive DN1p cluster 7.
source: Rh7 mRNA is present in this cluster as well as three others: the DN1as, DN2s, and the gl-positive DN1p cluster 7 (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The assignment of cluster 4 to the DN1ps is despite the lack of robust gl expression.
source: This assignment of cluster 4 to the DN1ps is despite the lack of robust gl expression and based in part on previous characterization of a Rh7 mimic line.
evidence: This is an inference based on Rh7 expression and prior knowledge.

claim: A Rh7 mimic line indicated that Rh7 may be only expressed in four to five DN1ps as well as the two DN1as.
source: This assignment of cluster 4 to the DN1ps is despite the lack of robust gl expression and based in part on previous characterization of a Rh7 mimic line. It indicated that Rh7 may be only expressed in four to five DN1ps as well as the two DN1as (Kistenpfennig et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A split-GAL4 line using regulatory regions of per and Rh7 indicated Rh7 expression in two DN1ps and the DN2 neurons.
source: To further assess Rh7 expression, we generated a split-GAL4 line using regulatory regions of per and Rh7; functional GAL4 should only be expressed in clock cells that also express Rh7. Consistent with the Rh7 mRNA expression pattern in the clusters, this assay also indicated Rh7 expression in two DN1ps and the DN2 neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the split-GAL4 data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: VGlut mRNA is enriched in most dorsal neuron clusters.
source: The glutamate vesicular transporter mRNA VGlut is enriched in most dorsal neuron clusters (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: A split-GAL4 assay with Pdfr and VGlut regulatory regions indicates that most DN1ps express VGlut.
source: Consistent with this conclusion is a split-GAL4 assay with Pdfr and VGlut regulatory regions: it indicates that most DN1ps express VGlut (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C); the RNA profiling indicates that only a single DN1p cluster—the gl-negative Rh7-positive cluster 4—is an exception.
evidence: This is supported by the split-GAL4 data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Only a single DN1p cluster—the gl-negative Rh7-positive cluster 4—does not express VGlut.
source: Consistent with this conclusion is a split-GAL4 assay with Pdfr and VGlut regulatory regions: it indicates that most DN1ps express VGlut (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C); the RNA profiling indicates that only a single DN1p cluster—the gl-negative Rh7-positive cluster 4—is an exception.
evidence: This is supported by the RNA profiling data.

claim: Some dorsal neurons are VGlut-positive, and glutamate expression is relevant to sleep-wake behavior.
source: These data are also consistent with prior studies indicating that some dorsal neurons are VGlut-positive, and glutamate expression is relevant to sleep-wake behavior (Guo et al., 2016; Guo et al., 2017; Hamasaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Six DN1p clusters were identified by known and newly identified markers.
source: In summary, six DN1p clusters were identified by the known and newly identified markers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a summary of the DN1p cluster identification.

claim: Clusters 14 and 20 are missing almost all marker genes identified in the better characterized clock neurons and were assigned to the DN3 population.
source: The two final clusters, 14 and 20, are missing almost all marker genes identified in the better characterized clock neurons and were therefore assigned to the enigmatic DN3 population.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of known marker genes.

claim: VGlut is expressed in Cluster 14.
source: The one exception is VGlut. It is expressed in Cluster 14, and previous studies have shown that some DN3s are glutamatergic (Hamasaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data and citation.

claim: Some DN3s are glutamatergic.
source: The one exception is VGlut. It is expressed in Cluster 14, and previous studies have shown that some DN3s are glutamatergic (Hamasaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Gene expression correlation analysis indicates that cluster 20 is similar to cluster 14.
source: Gene expression correlation analysis indicates that cluster 20 is similar to cluster 14 (Figure 3G), so we also assigned this last cluster to the DN3s.
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Cluster 20 is assigned to the DN3s.
source: Gene expression correlation analysis indicates that cluster 20 is similar to cluster 14 (Figure 3G), so we also assigned this last cluster to the DN3s.
evidence: This is an inference based on similarity to cluster 14.

claim: Each cluster shows a unique combination of marker gene expression.
source: Each cluster shows a unique combination of marker gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B, Source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmaps shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: TFs are prominently expressed in the clock clusters and extend well beyond the known clock gene TFs.
source: Notably, TFs are prominently expressed in the clock clusters and extend well beyond the known clock gene TFs, for example Figure 2.
evidence: This is supported by the TF expression data shown in Figure 5A and other figures.

claim: Some TF mRNAs are enriched in all clusters from a particular anatomical neuron group.
source: Interestingly, some TF mRNAs are enriched in all clusters from a particular anatomical neuron group (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ham, D, and gl transcripts are enriched in most DN1p clusters.
source: For example, ham, D as well as gl transcripts are enriched in most DN1p clusters (e.g. ham Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Each DN and LPN cluster has at least one TF mRNA enriched relative to the rest of the circadian network.
source: Most striking is the cluster-specific TF expression in the DNs and LPNs (labeled in yellow). Each cluster has at least one TF mRNA enriched relative to the rest of the circadian network (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cluster 4 DN1s show strong expression of transcripts encoding slou and so.
source: For example, cluster 4 DN1s show strong expression of transcripts encoding slou and so and the TF mRNAs hth, bi, toy, and Hr51 are enriched in all lateral neurons (e.g. toy and Hr51; Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data.

claim: The TF mRNAs hth, bi, toy, and Hr51 are enriched in all lateral neurons.
source: For example, cluster 4 DN1s show strong expression of transcripts encoding slou and so and the TF mRNAs hth, bi, toy, and Hr51 are enriched in all lateral neurons (e.g. toy and Hr51; Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: opa mRNA is specifically enriched in the LNvs.
source: opa mRNA is specifically enriched in the LNvs (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CrebA mRNA is highly expressed in only some s-LNv cluster cells due to robust oscillations under both LD and DD conditions.
source: Interestingly, CrebA mRNA is highly expressed in only some s-LNv cluster cells (Figure 5F; circle), due to robust oscillations under both LD and DD conditions (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: The amplitude of CrebA expression is more robust in DD than in LD.
source: For unknown reasons, the amplitude of CrebA expression is more robust in DD than in LD.
evidence: This is an observation from the cycling data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: pdm3 mRNA oscillates in the DN1p_CNMa cluster 1 with peak expression at midday.
source: pdm3 mRNA oscillates in the DN1p_CNMa cluster 1 with peak expression at midday (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 5H,I.

claim: ~24% of all transcripts identified in the 17 clock neuron clusters (1320/5517) undergo time-of-day oscillations in at least one cluster.
source: Although these conservative criteria were used to mitigate against false positive (see Materials and methods), ~24% of all transcripts identified in the 17 clock neuron clusters (1320/5517) undergo time-of-day oscillations in at least one cluster (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cycling analysis.

claim: 74% of the LD cycling transcripts are found in only one or two clusters.
source: Notably, even under the more cycling-permissive LD conditions, 74% of the LD cycling transcripts are found in only one or two clusters.
evidence: This is a finding from the cycling analysis.

claim: The two largest clusters (Clusters 1:DN1p_CNMa and 2_sLNv) have only ~30% overlap in cycling transcripts.
source: However, even the two largest clusters (Clusters 1:DN1p_CNMa and 2_sLNv) have only ~30% overlap.
evidence: This is a finding from the cycling analysis.

claim: Core clock gene transcripts are identified as cyclers in most of the 17 clusters in LD: Clk (11), tim (17), vri (12), and Pdp1 (13).
source: In contrast, the core clock gene transcripts are identified as cyclers in most of the 17 clusters in LD (Clk (11), tim (17), vri (12), and Pdp1 (13)).
evidence: This is a finding from the cycling analysis.

claim: Several other transcripts cycle in multiple clusters including the mRNA-binding protein fne, the arginine kinase ArgK, and the unknown transcript CG15628.
source: Several other transcripts also cycle in multiple clusters including the mRNA-binding protein fne, the arginine kinase ArgK, and the unknown transcript CG15628 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the cycling analysis.

claim: GO term analysis on LD cyclers from individual clusters was more informative for the larger clusters.
source: To address possible functions of the clock neurons cycling program, we first performed gene ontology (GO) term analysis on LD cyclers from the individual clusters (Supplementary file 2). This analysis was more informative for the larger clusters, as they had more cyclers than the smaller clusters.
evidence: This is an observation from the GO analysis.

claim: Many of the GO terms indicate that cycling transcripts contribute to different processes in the different clusters.
source: Although there are also significant GO terms shared between cyclers from different clusters such as behavior, neuron projection morphogenesis and G-protein-coupled signaling pathways, many of the GO terms indicate that cycling transcripts contribute to different processes in the different clusters.
evidence: This is a finding from the GO analysis.

claim: The DN1p_CNMa cyclers (cluster 1) are enriched for chemical synaptic transmission (0.008).
source: For example, the DN1p_CNMa cyclers (cluster 1) are enriched for chemical synaptic transmission (0.008), whereas the s-LNv cyclers (cluster 2) are enriched for cation membrane transport (2.1E-7).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO analysis.

claim: The s-LNv cyclers (cluster 2) are enriched for cation membrane transport (2.1E-7).
source: For example, the DN1p_CNMa cyclers (cluster 1) are enriched for chemical synaptic transmission (0.008), whereas the s-LNv cyclers (cluster 2) are enriched for cation membrane transport (2.1E-7).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO analysis.

claim: GO term analysis on all cycling transcripts identified in any of the 17 clusters revealed new GO terms including second messenger-mediated signaling, cell-cell adhesion via plasma membrane adhesion molecules and axonogenesis.
source: We also performed GO term analysis on all cycling transcripts identified in any of the 17 clusters (Supplementary file 3). In addition to the GO terms identified in multiple individual clusters (Figure 6A, Asterix), several new GO terms emerged from the combined cyclers; they included second messenger-mediated signaling, cell-cell adhesion via plasma membrane adhesion molecules and axonogenesis (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the combined GO analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: These new GO terms required the pooling of cycling transcripts because each clock neuron cluster only contains one or two cycling transcripts from these large gene families.
source: These new functions required the pooling of cycling transcripts because each clock neuron cluster only contains one or two cycling transcripts from these large gene families.
evidence: This is an explanation for why the combined analysis was necessary.

claim: In LD, G-protein-coupled receptor signaling was identified as a GO term only for cycling transcripts that peak at night.
source: Interestingly, in LD, G-protein-coupled receptor signaling was identified as a GO term only for cycling transcripts that peak at night.
evidence: This is a finding from the time-of-day specific GO analysis.

claim: Neuron-projection morphogenesis was identified as a GO term only for cycling transcripts peaking during the day.
source: In contrast neuron-projection morphogenesis was identified as a GO term only for cycling transcripts peaking during the day.
evidence: This is a finding from the time-of-day specific GO analysis.

claim: Four of 11 DIP transcripts are specifically enriched and undergo LD cycling in specific clock neuron clusters.
source: Two prominent examples of the axonogenesis category are the DIP (Dpr interacting proteins; 11 genes) and Dpr (Defective proboscis extension response; 21 genes) families. A DIP protein on the surface of a neuron has affinity for partner Dpr proteins, which together help drive synapse specificity during development (Cosmanescu et al., 2018). Four of 11 DIP transcripts are specifically enriched and undergo LD cycling in specific clock neuron clusters (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 10 of 21 Dpr transcripts are enriched and undergo LD cycling in specific clusters.
source: Similarly, 10 of 21 Dpr transcripts are enriched and undergo LD cycling in specific clusters (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: DIP-beta mRNA is enriched and cycles strongly in s-LNvs.
source: Intriguingly, DIP-beta mRNA is enriched and cycles strongly in s-LNvs (Figure 6C,D), whereas a Dpr8 transcript encodes one of its partner proteins and cycles with a similar phase in DN1ps (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Dpr8 transcript encodes one of DIP-beta's partner proteins and cycles with a similar phase in DN1ps.
source: Intriguingly, DIP-beta mRNA is enriched and cycles strongly in s-LNvs (Figure 6C,D), whereas a Dpr8 transcript encodes one of its partner proteins and cycles with a similar phase in DN1ps (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Cycling gene expression regulation of DIP-beta and Dpr8 may contribute to the circadian regulation of the known interaction between s-LNvs and DN1ps.
source: Perhaps, cycling gene expression regulation of DIP-beta and Dpr8 contribute to the circadian regulation of the known interaction between s-LNvs and DN1ps.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cycling DIP-beta and Dpr8 data.

claim: Circadian regulation of an interaction between s-LNv termini and a target like DN1ps was the original suggestion for the function of s-LNv morphological cycling.
source: Circadian regulation of an interaction between s-LNv termini and a target like DN1ps was the original suggestion for the function of s-LNv morphological cycling (Fernández et al., 2008; Petsakou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Beat transcripts encode another Ig superfamily of molecules involved in axonogenesis and show impressive cluster-specific enrichment and cycling.
source: Beat transcripts encode another Ig superfamily of molecules, which are involved in axonogenesis (Pipes et al., 2001) and show impressive cluster-specific enrichment and cycling (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is supported by the expression and cycling data shown in Figure 6F,G and citation.

claim: DIP, Dpr, and Beat family cell surface molecules may help temporally coordinate synaptic contacts within the circadian circuit and elsewhere within the brain to superimpose time-of-day control on synaptic strength if not choice.
source: We speculate that all three classes of cell surface molecules help temporally coordinate synaptic contacts, principles that function broadly within the circadian circuit and even elsewhere within the brain to superimpose time-of-day control on synaptic strength if not choice (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cycling cell-surface molecule data.

claim: The identification of the 17 clock clusters reflects gene expression heterogeneity revealed by the modified CEL-Seq2 method.
source: We suspect that the identification of the 17 clock clusters reflects gene expression heterogeneity revealed by our modified CEL-Seq2 method.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clustering results.

claim: A large number of genes and UMIs resulted from the method, which probably allowed for a more thorough definition of clock neuron cell type.
source: A large number of genes and UMIs resulted, which probably allowed for a more thorough definition of clock neuron cell type.
evidence: This is an inference based on the sequencing depth achieved.

claim: The only fly brain neuron studies with similar sequencing depth per cell also reported comparable molecular heterogeneity.
source: The only fly brain neuron studies with similar sequencing depth per cell also reported comparable molecular heterogeneity (Li et al., 2020; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: The 39 clusters indicates about 1–2 cells/cluster from each side of the brain at about 8X coverage for each cell at each time point.
source: Assuming the immunostaining revealed all GFP-positive neurons (Figure 1A), the 39 clusters indicates about 1–2 cells/cluster from each side of the brain at about 8X coverage for each cell at each time point (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the number of clusters and cells.

claim: Many of the small clusters may be DN3 neurons that were inefficiently recovered during FACS sorting, due perhaps to lower Clk expression.
source: One possibility is that many of the small clusters are DN3 neurons that were inefficiently recovered during FACS sorting, due perhaps to lower Clk expression (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the small clusters.

claim: The 17 final clock neuron groups contain about two to three cells per cluster.
source: The 17 final clock neuron groups contain a somewhat larger number of cells per cluster, about two to three, many of which are well-defined by immunohistochemistry and contain the predicted number of cells.
evidence: This is a description of the final cluster composition.

claim: The two DN1as, two LNd_Trissin cells, two DN2s, and the four s-LNvs contain the predicted number of cells.
source: They include for example the two DN1as, two LNd_Trissin cells, two DN2s, and the four s-LNvs.
evidence: This is a description of clusters that match expected cell numbers.

claim: Clusters for l-LNvs and LPNs contain too few cells.
source: There are, however, clusters that contain too few cells, most notably the l-LNvs and the LPNs; they should contain four and three cells, respectively.
evidence: This is an observation about clusters with fewer cells than expected.

claim: Many l-LNv and LPN neurons are probably poorly recovered or perhaps incorrectly assigned.
source: As the correct cell numbers of l-LNvs and LPNs are easily visible by GFP-staining of Clk856-GAL4 > UAS-Stinger-GFP brains, many of these neurons are probably poorly recovered or perhaps incorrectly assigned.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy in cell numbers.

claim: The clustering and analysis clarified several clock neuron identity issues for the LNds and the DN1ps.
source: The clustering and analysis clarified several clock neuron identity issues for the LNds and the DN1ps.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the findings.

claim: The ITP-positive LNd and the fifth s-LNv have nearly identical properties; they innervate the same brain areas with similar pre- and postsynaptic sites, and they both drive evening activity.
source: Their indistinguishable gene expression profiles fit nicely with recent neuroanatomical studies suggesting that they have nearly identical properties; they innervate the same brain areas with similar pre- and postsynaptic sites, and they both drive evening activity (Schubert et al., 2018; Hermann-Luibl et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The division of the DN1ps into six clusters was surprising.
source: Most surprising perhaps was the division of the DN1ps into six clusters.
evidence: This is a statement about the unexpected finding.

claim: Two DN1p clusters express the rhodopsin gene Rh7, and two others express the neuropeptides CNMa and Dh31.
source: Two of these express the recently characterized rhodopsin gene Rh7, and two others the neuropeptides CNMa and Dh31.
evidence: This is a summary of the DN1p cluster characteristics.

claim: All the CNMa cells reside close together in the dorsal brain and are spatially distinct from the rest of the DN1p population.
source: All the CNMa cells reside close together in the dorsal brain and are spatially distinct from the rest of the DN1p population, yet they are still divided into two clusters based on this molecular profiling.
evidence: This is an observation about the spatial organization of CNMa-expressing cells.

claim: Two recently identified sleep-promoting DN1p groups show novel projection patterns and should be relevant to the DN1p clusters.
source: Two recently identified sleep-promoting DN1p groups show novel projection patterns and should be relevant (Guo et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2016), but we do not know which DN1p clusters they define.
evidence: This is a statement about the relevance of recent findings to the current study, supported by citations.

claim: Additional post-transcriptional regulation might be important for neuronal function.
source: Nonetheless, additional post-transcriptional regulation might also be important for neuronal function.
evidence: This is a speculation about the role of post-transcriptional regulation.

claim: AstC-R2 is reported to be expressed in only one LNd, yet its mRNA is expressed in both clusters 9 and 12.
source: For instance, AstC-R2 is reported to be expressed in only one LNd (Díaz et al., 2019), yet its mRNA is expressed in both clusters 9 and 12.
evidence: This is an observation of a discrepancy between the current data and a previous report.

claim: AstC-R2 transcript (as well as others) may undergo post-transcriptional regulation that further refines protein expression within the clock neuron network.
source: We speculate that this transcript (as well as others) may undergo post-transcriptional regulation that further refines protein expression within the clock neuron network.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy.

claim: There is abundant circadian regulation of mRNA cycling in the 17 clock neuron clusters.
source: There is abundant circadian regulation of mRNA cycling in the 17 clock neuron clusters.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the cycling analysis.

claim: The canonical property of clock gene cycling is not present in all 17 clusters by computational criteria.
source: It is therefore surprising that the canonical property of clock gene cycling is not present in all of them.
evidence: This is an observation about the cycling analysis results.

claim: vri and tim mRNA cycle in all 17 clusters by eye.
source: However, vri and tim mRNA cycle in all 17 clusters by eye (also see Figure 2), suggesting that the lack of universal clock gene cycling reflects some data variability combined with the conservative computational criteria used to define cycling.
evidence: This is an observation from visual inspection of the data.

claim: The lack of universal clock gene cycling reflects some data variability combined with the conservative computational criteria used to define cycling.
source: However, vri and tim mRNA cycle in all 17 clusters by eye (also see Figure 2), suggesting that the lack of universal clock gene cycling reflects some data variability combined with the conservative computational criteria used to define cycling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why clock genes don't meet cycling criteria in all clusters.

claim: Most non-clock gene mRNA cycling remains highly neuron-specific by eye as well as by computation.
source: In contrast and with only a few exceptions, most non-clock gene mRNA cycling remains highly neuron-specific by eye as well as by computation.
evidence: This is an observation about the specificity of non-clock gene cycling.

claim: A previous bulk sequencing study of three categories of clock neurons came to a similar conclusion about neuron-specific cycling.
source: Although so much neuron-specific cycling in these 17 clusters of clock neurons might seem surprising, our previous bulk sequencing study of three categories of clock neurons (PDF cells, LNds, and DN1s) came to a similar conclusion (Abruzzi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The large percentage of neuron-specific cycling probably reflects some specific temporal as well as spatial gene expression regulation occurring within clock neurons.
source: The large percentage probably reflects some specific temporal as well as spatial gene expression regulation occurring within clock neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cycling data.

claim: Circadian regulation of gene expression is highly cell- and tissue-specific with only the exception of core clock genes and a handful of others.
source: However, this neuron-specific control recapitulates lessons learned from mammals as well as from flies about the circadian regulation of gene expression: this regulation is highly cell- and tissue-specific with only the exception of core clock genes and a handful of others.
evidence: This is established knowledge about circadian gene regulation.

claim: The mammalian brain has the lowest number of tissue-specific cycling transcripts.
source: In this context of cell type and tissue, it is interesting that the mammalian brain has the lowest number of tissue-specific cycling transcripts (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The mammalian brain may have the lowest number of tissue-specific cycling transcripts because it has the greatest number of constituent cell types.
source: Perhaps, this is because the brain has the greatest number of constituent cell types.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observation.

claim: Without assaying separately the constituent cells of the brain, cell-specific cycling is invisible when assaying the complete tissue/organ.
source: Without assaying separately these cells, cell-specific cycling is invisible when assaying the complete tissue/organ.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of bulk tissue analysis.

claim: Most of the cycling mRNAs identified in this study were not detected as cycling in fly head or brain mRNA.
source: In this context, most of the cycling mRNAs identified in this study were not detected as cycling in fly head or brain mRNA (Hughes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A single-cell RNA sequencing study of the mouse SCN identified only five neuronal subtypes.
source: While this work was in progress, we became aware of a single-cell RNA sequencing study of the mouse SCN, the mammalian equivalent of the 150 fly clock neurons (Wen et al., 2020). Although only five neuronal subtypes were identified, this number is consistent with previous characterizations of SCN neuronal heterogeneity (Welsh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: SCN neuronal heterogeneity may be underestimated due to the lower sequencing depth afforded by droplet-based methods.
source: It is also possible that this heterogeneity is underestimated due to the lower sequencing depth afforded by droplet-based methods (Wen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculation about the limitations of droplet-based methods, supported by citation.

claim: High-throughput commercial sequencing methods may underestimate neuronal heterogeneity because of limited sequencing depth.
source: We suspect that high-throughput commercial sequencing methods similarly underestimate neuronal heterogeneity because of limited sequencing depth.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the comparison of sequencing methods.

claim: High-throughput commercial methods only identified 29 and 87 initial clusters in larval and adult Drosophila brains.
source: For example, they only identified 29 and 87 initial clusters in larval and adult Drosophila brains (Davie et al., 2018; Brunet Avalos et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: This work reveals a surprising extent of fly brain clock neuron heterogeneity.
source: In summary, this work reveals a surprising extent of fly brain clock neuron heterogeneity and provides a resource for future functional and mechanistic circadian studies.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the main finding.

claim: This work provides a resource for future functional and mechanistic circadian studies.
source: In summary, this work reveals a surprising extent of fly brain clock neuron heterogeneity and provides a resource for future functional and mechanistic circadian studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the study.

claim: Neuronal heterogeneity will be more generally characteristic of fly brain circuits.
source: Although some of these features may be limited to the clock system, we suspect that neuronal heterogeneity will be more generally characteristic of fly brain circuits.
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: Neuronal heterogeneity helps explain why Drosophila has such a sophisticated behavioral repertoire despite a brain of only 100,000 neurons.
source: This heterogeneity also helps explain why Drosophila has such a sophisticated behavioral repertoire despite a brain of only 100,000 neurons and suggests that many drivers that express in one or only a few neurons are likely to have substantial behavioral impact.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of neuronal heterogeneity.

claim: Many drivers that express in one or only a few neurons are likely to have substantial behavioral impact.
source: This heterogeneity also helps explain why Drosophila has such a sophisticated behavioral repertoire despite a brain of only 100,000 neurons and suggests that many drivers that express in one or only a few neurons are likely to have substantial behavioral impact.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of specific neuronal drivers.
